marks.gloss_en: לתוך עוגה של מים נמי אמרי: לבבואה קא שחיט! -- into a pool too they will say: he slaughters to his reflection
בעכורים שנו -- they taught it of murky water (= p_okimta_achurim); 'which shows no reflection' is Steinsaltz's explanation
why not into seas? because they will say: he is slaughtering to the angel of the sea
so that he will not emulate the heretics
אשם תלוי בר נידר ונידב הוא? -- the mishna lists asham talui among what is vowed or donated
הא מני? רבי אלעזר היא, דאמר: מתנדב אדם אשם תלוי בכל יום
R' Yochanan: whose is this [mishna]? It is R' Elazar's
פסח בר נידב ונידר הוא? זמנא קביעא ליה! -- pesach has a fixed time
שאני פסח, הואיל והפרשתו כל השנה כולה
R' Oshaya: pesach is different, since its designation is [possible] the whole year
one who slaughters for the sake of an olah, zevachim, asham talui, pesach, or todah -- his slaughter is invalid
this is the principle: whatever is vowed or donated -- one who slaughters for its sake, [the animal] is forbidden
R' Yannai: they taught [the invalidation] only of unblemished animals
תניא כוותיה דרבא -- the baraita states the outside-the-hole procedure for one who would clean his courtyard, as Rava read the mishna
one travelling on a ship with no place to slaughter puts his hand outside the ship and slaughters, the blood running down the ship's sides
והא אמרת אין שוחטין לגומא כלל? -- how may he make a hole in his house, if one may not slaughter into a hole at all? (Abaye first answered: the first clause is the marketplace -- refuted at 41b.4)
one may not slaughter into a hole [in the ground] at all
אלא אמר רבא הכי קאמר: not into the hole itself at all; in the house one slaughters at a place outside the hole and the blood runs into it
Rava: the mishna means -- not into a hole at all; one who wants to clean his courtyard makes a place outside the hole and slaughters, the blood running down into the hole
מדקתני סיפא ובשוק לא יעשה כן, מכלל דרישא לאו בשוק עסקינן -- the latter clause names the marketplace, so the first clause is not about it
[in the marketplace not] because it is said 'and in their statutes you shall not walk' (Lev 18:3)
והא לא קאמר ״לשם חטאתי״? -- but he did not say 'for the sake of MY sin offering'
באומר ״לשם חטאתי״ -- where he says 'for the sake of my sin offering' (= p_abbahu_beomer_chatati)
R' Yochanan: they taught this only of one who is not liable to a sin offering
the mishnah: one who slaughters for the sake of a sin offering -- his slaughter is valid
והא לא קאמר ״לשם תמורת זבחי״? -- but he did not say 'for the sake of the substitute of MY offering'
באומר ״לשם תמורת זבחי״ -- where he says 'for the sake of the substitute of my offering' (= p_abbahu_beomer_temurat_zivchi)
R' Elazar: they taught this only where he has no offering inside his house
והא לא קאמר ״לשם עולת אשתי״? -- but he did not say 'for the sake of MY WIFE's burnt offering'
באומר ״לשם עולת אשתי״ -- where he says 'for the sake of my wife's burnt offering' (= p_abbahu_beomer_olat_ishti)
R' Elazar: they taught this only where he has no wife
'and what is not vowed or donated' -- to include the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth
[the rule comes] to include the burnt offering of a nazirite
